key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr combined the lowest measured wear rate with the best corrosion resistance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-exposed 304 stainless steel components, HVAF is a promising coating route when both properties matter.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compare microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction and volume wear rates.
Evaluate corrosion potential, current density and corrosion resistance.
evidence_signal: HVAF reduced volume wear rate from (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for bare steel to (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) and achieved the lowest corrosion current density, 1.75±0.02 μA/cm², among the coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct transfer of the rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
